The crash itself came from a long run up in share prices funded heavily by borrowing, so when prices turned the margin calls forced more selling and the fall fed itself. What turned it into a depression was mostly what happened afterwards. Banks failed in waves and nobody stood behind depositors, so the money supply contracted sharply. Central banks stayed tied to gold and raised rates when they should have cut. Governments cut spending to balance budgets into a slump, and tariffs like Smoot-Hawley shrank trade further. So the crash was the trigger and the policy response was the reason it lasted.

what causes tides, briefly

Mostly the moon pulling on the oceans, with the sun adding a smaller pull that sometimes lines up and sometimes cancels out. The near side bulges towards the moon and the far side bulges away, which is why you get two high tides a day rather than one. When the sun and moon line up you get the big spring tides, and when they sit at right angles you get the weak neap ones.
alright. why is the sky red at sunset and not at noon

Sunlight scatters off air molecules, and the short blue wavelengths scatter far more than the long red ones. At noon the light comes almost straight down through a thin slice of atmosphere, so plenty of blue survives and reaches you from every direction. At sunset it travels a long slanted path, the blue is scattered away before it arrives, and what's left is the red and orange end.
